transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you all for being here. As you know, our exhibition of original costumes from the studio's films opens to the public this Saturday, and I'll be making the final approval decision on the public-opening package after our review today. The venue has proposed an open-gallery display with visitor photography, standard gallery lighting, a 90-person hourly capacity, and three floor attendants. I'd like to go through this proposal with each of you — registrar, conservator, accessibility coordinator, and security manager — to hear your assessments before I make my decision. Let's start with you — what are your thoughts on the proposed display approach?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Maya, before we go further on the display approach, I need to flag something critical. I reviewed the executed loan agreement this morning, and it contains several terms that directly conflict with the venue's proposal. Every borrowed costume must be displayed in a locked vitrine — not an open-gallery display. Visitor photography is explicitly prohibited. And the lender credit must read exactly 'Costumes courtesy of the Meridian Film Archive.' I have not yet entered these terms into the opening checklist, but they are binding obligations we cannot override.
